title: Holistic asset class preferences - Barclays Private Bank
text: Barclays Home Contact us Log in Menu Holistic asset class preferences MULTI-ASSET PORTFOLIO ALLOCATION 9 October 2026 Julien Lafargue, CFA, Chief Market Strategist Share this Insight Share page via Facebook Share page via X Share page via LinkedIn Share page via email High-level allocation After this month's review, we remain neutral at the asset class level and our allocation is unchanged We would still rather add risk on market pullbacks than cut exposure On tactical grounds, we continue to recommend holding slightly more cash than usual. Fixed income Our overall stance on fixed income stays broadly neutral, but within it we still prefer investment grade to high yield bonds Spreads look asymmetric to us. There is little room for them to tighten further, but they could widen sharply if the global economy weakens faster than expected We continue to find emerging market debt attractive. Yields are elevated and in many cases fundamentals match or beat those of developed market peers Yields have jumped in recent months, but we are keeping duration neutral in the EU and UK (4-6 years) and a slightly cautious view in the US (3-5 years) as we expect more volatility. Our bias would be to add to duration over time. Equities Equities are still the main driver of portfolio growth We remain neutral at the index level and focus on regional and sector opportunities. Following their strong outperformance, we have recently neutralised our constructive exposure to the global healthcare sector. At the same time, we upgraded global communication services from a cautious stance after a period of significant underperformance In our view, US equities still appear expensive and positioning remains unfavourable. However, we are constructive on the AI complex, so keep a neutral exposure to the region. Regionally, emerging markets have lagged since mid-June and still offer better value, in our view. Alternatives We keep a positive bias towards hedge funds and private markets for their diversification benefits, while staying highly selective We remain broadly neutral on commodities. We see them as a source of trading opportunities rather than a major driver of long-term returns Indeed, gold’s rebound has been short-lived, as Washington has so far failed to keep long-term yields under control. That said, from a portfolio construction perspective, we see benefits in maintaining some exposure to the precious metal. Portfolio strategy We believe portfolios should be deliberately neutral but built to limit downside risk while capturing as much upside as possible. That means a resilient core, clear ways to add risk during drawdowns and explicit protection that can be used opportunistically in dislocated markets A core-satellite approach still makes sense to us. Passive exposure helps contain index concentration risk, while active strategies can take advantage of the high dispersion we see within asset classes Option overlays, used directly or through structured solutions, can further improve the risk-reward profile in a fast-moving, narrative-driven market.
